title: What If You Drilled Straight Into Magma?

scenes.text: What if you drilled into magma? Someone did, by accident, and the result was not a volcano.
In 2009, a geothermal drill in Iceland was lowered about 2,100 meters down, and suddenly hit rock melted at 900 to 1,000 degrees Celsius.
The hole did not erupt. Instead, steam roared up at over 450 degrees, a world record for geothermal heat.
Engineers kept the hole open with a perforated steel casing, and superheated steam flowed for about two years.
That one well could have powered roughly 36 megawatts, more than half of the whole Krafla power plant.
So the real danger of hitting magma is not an explosion. It's that a valve failed first, and the hole had to be stoppered.
